summary.short: Amends New York Civil Rights Law §50-f on post-mortem publicity rights. Defines digital replicas and makes unauthorized knowing use of a deceased performer's digital replica in audiovisual works, sound recordings or live musical performances actionable for damages, subject to exceptions. Takes effect immediately.
summary.long: The bill amends subdivisions 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 10 of Civil Rights Law §50-f on rights in deceased personalities' name, voice, signature, photograph or likeness. Its amended definitions cover deceased performers and personalities domiciled in New York at death, and describe a digital replica as a highly realistic, readily identifiable computer-generated representation of an individual's voice or visual likeness. Subdivision 2(b) makes a person liable for damages for knowingly using a deceased performer's digital replica without authorization or prior consent in an audiovisual work, sound recording or live musical performance. Subdivision 2(c) sets liability at the greater of $2,000 or compensatory damages plus unauthorized profits, and allows punitive damages. Subdivision 2(d) revises exemptions, including for docudramas and self-portrayals with some fictionalization, except in live musical performances. Subdivision 9 adds streaming services to the advertising media whose owners and employees are exempt absent actual knowledge by prior notification. Subdivision 10 keeps the exemption for services selling visual works unless the person received a successor's notice of an unauthorized digital replica and did not promptly remove it. The act takes effect immediately.

thresholds.note: The only numeric amount is the statutory minimum damages of two thousand dollars in Section 1 (civil rights law 50-f(2)(c)(i)), a remedy amount that sets a damages floor rather than a cutoff changing legal treatment, so it is recorded under enforcement rather than thresholds. The text contains no size, age, value or volume cutoffs.
